postings.title: U.S. Government Seeks to Lease Office Space in San Juan, Puerto Rico
postings.office: PBS R00 CENTER FOR BROKER SERVICES

pass1.summary: GSA lease solicitation for about 2,080 to 2,184 sq ft of office space in San Juan with clear requirements and a November 2026 deadline. Minor typo ('Head West om PR 2') and a reference to USTP staff with no explanation. The map and delineated area are in an attachment.

Navy RFQ for a valve stem (TTV) with a clear title and a deadline extended to 30 Nov 2026 by amendment. The posting body is mostly boilerplate and typos ('PERPARDENESS', 'ORDER OR PRECEDENCE'). Quantity and item detail depend on attachments.

Navy presolicitation for a self-locking nut with a clear NSN-style title, a routine parts buy. Quantity and item detail are not in the body and depend on attachments; the text is otherwise boilerplate.
Sole-source notice for a valve (NSN) that clearly states what and why. The 440-day window is just an administrative artifact, and the 45-day response language is standard.

postings.title: SPACER, 2ND STAGE

pass1.summary: The spacer posting is stacked with conflicting amendment history. One note says quotes are due 20 NOV 2025, another says the new date is 23 JUN 2026, and the posted deadline is 2026-11-16. It also cites a total small business set-aside clause while the set-aside is listed as none. The drawing note is garbled ("gives yDrawings"). A bidder cannot tell the real due date or set-aside status.

postings.title: BOLT,MACHINE

The place or places of performance may not be changed without the authorization of the Procurement Contracting Officer. Upon receipt of this order, promptly notify the Government representative who normally services your plant so that appropriate planning for Government inspection can be accomplished. If you do not have an assigned Government representative, notify the nearest Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) Office. In the event that a local Government representative or DCMA Office cannot be located, our purchasing agent should be notified immediately. 3.12.5 Any changes made by the Contractor to a qualified quality system will require re-submittal to the PCO and concurrence by the Government Quality Assurance Representative prior to adoption. 3.13 Contractor Inspection Requirements - The Contractor must maintain adequate records of all inspections and tests. When conditions warrant, the supplier's personnel must be made available for operations of such devices and for verification of their accuracy and condition. 3.13.2 All documents and reference data applicable to this contract must be available for review by the Government representative. Copies of documents required for Government inspection purposes must be furnished in accordance with the instructions provided by the Government representative. 3.14 Subcontractor Inspection Requirements - The Government has the right to inspect at source, any supplies or services that were not manufactured or performed within the contractor's facility. postings.description: This notice serves as formal notification that Request for Quote (RFQ) No. 6923G526Q0051 for the drydocking and American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) Special Periodical Survey of the M/V Seaway Guardian is hereby cancelled in its entirety. The Government is reevaluating its acquisition strategy and operational timeline, and intends to resolicit this requirement in 2027. A new solicitation number will be issued at that time, and interested vendors should monitor SAM.gov for future postings regarding this effort. No contract award will be made from this solicitation. A00004 - The purpose of this amendment is to: 1. Extend the quotation due date to 10/02/2026 at 12:00 PM EST. //NOTHING FOLLOWS// A00003 - The purpose of this amendment is to: 1. Extend the quotation due date to 9/25/2026 at 2:00 PM EST. 2. All other terms and conditions remain unchanged. //NOTHING FOLLOWS// A00002 - The purpose of this amendment is to: 1. Incorporate additional questions and answers. 2. Incorporate Seaway Guardian overboard valves and seachest list. 3. Extend the quotation due date to September 18, 2026 at 2:00 PM EST. //NOTHING FOLLOWS// A00001 - The purpose of this amendment is to: 1. Incorporate the questions & answers. 2. The quotation due date remains unchanged. //NOTHING FOLLOWS// This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with the Format in Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested, and a written solicitation will not be issued. The solicitation is issued as a Request for Quote (RFQ). This solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular FAC 2026-01 dated March 13, 2026. This requirement is being solicited as full and open competition using FAR (RFO) Part 12 Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. The NAICS Code is 336611 – Ship Building and Repairing. The solicitation number is 6923G526Q0051. **NOTE: Quoters must be registered in SAM.gov and have an active registration at the time of this solicitation closing. SCHEDULE OF SUPPLIES/SERVICES: See Attachment B –Pricing Sheet. DESCRIPTION OF WORK: The Great Lakes St. Lawrence Seaway Development Corporation (GLS) has a requirement to complete a drydocking and American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) Classification Society first 5-year special periodical associated surveys of the marine motor vessel (M/V) “Seaway Guardian.” This will include the drydocking of the vessel, ABS special periodical hull, machinery, and automation surveys, renewal of load line, IAPP, and IOPP certification as well as additional maintenance, steel work, and coating renewal. The work shall be completed at the contractor’s marine maintenance and repair facility (shipyard). All in exact accordance with this solicitation and attached Statement of Work (SOW). CONTRACT TYPE: This solicitation is a Request for Quote (RFQ) that will result in the award of a firm fixed price contract under FAR Part 12, subject to the availability of funds. CONTRACT PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: The contractor shall begin performance within 30 calendar days and complete within 60 calendar days after receiving the Notice to Proceed (NTP). It is expected that the notice to proceed will be issued in September 2026. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE/ACCEPTANCE: All work is to be completed at the contractor’s marine maintenance and repair facility (shipyard). While the vessel is out of the water, ESD NOLA shall replace the existing fathometer system (including hull transducer and display/processing units as applicable). 4.1.2 Background The ANT Colfax 64’ ANB requires an operational fathometer for safe navigation during its Aids to Navigation mission. The current system is inoperable, requiring a complete replacement that necessitates drydocking or hoisting the vessel out of the water to access the hull penetrations. 4.2 Specific Tasks and Requirements The Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, and facilities necessary to perform the following tasks, unless specifically noted as Government Furnished Equipment (GFE): Task 2.1: Haul-Out & Blocking: The Contractor shall haul out the 64’ ANB using a travel lift, marine railway, or drydock capable of safely handling the vessel’s weight and dimensions. Task 2.7: Relaunch: Upon completion of the installation and initial visual inspection, the Contractor shall lift and relaunch the vessel into the water. The Contractor shall leave the vessel in the slings/blocks in the water for a sufficient time to inspect the new hull penetration for any leaks before final release. 4.2.8 Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) Fathometer System: The USCG ESD NOLA has the new fathometer system. Vessel Delivery: USCG personnel will deliver the 64’ ANB to the Contractor’s facility and operate the vessel during sea trials. 4.2.9 Quality Assurance and Testing Watertight Integrity Test: Prior to final acceptance, ANT Colfax and ESD NOLA will visually inspect the transducer hull penetration while the vessel is in the water to verify there is zero water ingress. Overview The General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service (PBS), is conducting market research to establish Multiple-Award Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contracts for comprehensive, multidisciplinary Architect-Engineer (A/E) services. These contracts are intended to provide integrated, sustainable, and adaptive design solutions across federally owned and leased real property nationwide. The Government anticipates awarding multiple contracts with multi-year ordering periods (5 year base with one 5 year option) to support GSA zones and client agencies across the United States and its territories. Expected typical project size is to be above the simplified acquisition threshold of $350,000. The potential place of performance for services rendered under this contract is on an as-needed basis for federal projects anywhere in the United States and its territories. This will require the capability to travel to GSA and other Government agency office locations nationwide. In some instances, performance of services is expected to require the capability for contractors to dispatch personnel to multiple locations simultaneously. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 541310 (Architectural Services) & 541330 (Engineering Services), which has a small business size standard of $12.5 million and $25.5 million respectively. Scope of Services Services provided under the resulting IDIQ contracts will encompass a comprehensive range of professional A/E design and engineering disciplines. Scopes of work for individual task orders may include, but are not limited to, the following: 1. Core Project Life Cycle Services - These services cover the entire project lifecycle, from initial concept to post-construction closeout. Planning and Pre-Design Feasibility, pre-design, and project development studies Master planning Cost Estimating Real Estate Market Analysis Assessment and Investigation Existing conditions surveys, and field investigation Building condition survey evaluation reports (exterior and interior) Environmental investigation, reviews, inventories, and audits Energy audits and studies Design and Documentation Concept design, Design development, and Construction document development (both architectural and engineering) Interior design, including Furniture, Fixtures, and Equipment (FFE) Building standard documents Construction Support and Closeout Constructability review and evaluation Submittal and shop drawing review Management and inspection (M&I) services during construction and Construction inspection Building and system commissioning Post Construction Contract Services (PCCS); Record and close-out documents 2. Specialized Technical & System Design - Work requested often involves the assessment, repair, and upgrade of existing complex building systems. Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing (MEP) Full MEP services, including design of HVAC systems and electrical systems and lighting Assessment and design for mechanical components (e.g., pumps, fans, air handlers, water distribution systems) and air distribution Design of water and waste water systems, including performance of sanitary inspections Temperature control assessment and design and BAS system assessment and integration Building Structure and Envelope Structural evaluation and design Façade evaluation and remediation design Water infiltration investigation and mitigation design Safety, Security, and Compliance Fire and Life Safety evaluation and design Rehabs to improve energy efficiency and safety concerns Seismic & Blast protection and Vertical Transportation Code Compliance 3. Required AE Disciplines and Expertise - AE firms will need staff with licensed and/or specialized expertise in the following disciplines: Core Architectural and Engineering Disciplines Architecture and Interior Architecture Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Structural & Civil Engineering, and Plumbing Historic Preservation Specialized Expertise A Qualified/Licensed Fire Protection Engineer (NCEES)* Security Space Planning & Workplace Cost Estimating and Scheduling Environmental Services Modernization and Quality Control Building Information Modeling (BIM) Quality control review and Report writing Submission Requirements Interested firms are invited to submit a written Capability Statement. Submissions must not exceed five (5) pages in length and must address the following elements: A. Company Profile Official company name, street address, telephone number, and primary website URL. Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code. Office location(s) and primary design production facilities. Business size status under NAICS 541310 or 541330 (Large Business or Small Business). Applicable SBA socio-economic certifications (e.g., 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business [SDVOSB], Woman-Owned Small Business [WOSB], or Economically Disadvantaged WOSB [EDWOSB]). B. Relevant Experience Summarize three to five (3–5) relevant projects completed within the past ten (10) years. Demonstrate experience in projects of similar scale, scope, and complexity, such as federal workplace design, major repairs and alterations, or complex building systems. Include project title, customer/agency point of contact, contract value, role (Prime or Subcontractor), and a brief narrative of the work performed. C. Nationwide Capacity Demonstrate organizational capacity to manage and execute multiple task orders simultaneously across diverse geographic locations nationwide. Describe key disciplines maintained in-house versus those typically fulfilled through subcontractor or joint venture arrangements. Submission Instructions Responses must be submitted electronically via email to the primary procurement contacts listed below: Submission Deadline: Primary Contact: Point of Contact Email: Subject Line Format: Sources Sought Response - National A/E IDIQ - [Firm Name] Hard copies, telephonic inquiries, and late submissions will not be reviewed or acknowledged. All information provided in response to this notice will be used strictly for market research and acquisition planning purposes. This notice encourages participation from qualified small business concerns, including socio-economic program participants, to assist GSA in evaluating the feasibility of small business set-asides for this procurement. All prospective offerors are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for updates, future notices, or potential solicitations related to this requirement.

postings.description: Description This is a solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 75110PR270000099 is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ) for the seven-month rental, maintenance, repair, replacement, training, and LPG fuel support of one 6,000-pound forklift and one 12,000-pound forklift at USCG TRACEN Birmingham-Southern. This acquisition IS set aside for small business concerns. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-01 Effective Date 03/13/2026. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 532490, with a small business size standard of $40.0. Product Service Code is W039. Submission of offers. Submit signed and dated offers to the office specified in this solicitation at or before the exact time specified in this solicitation. As a minimum, offers shall include— (1) The solicitation number. (2) The name, address, telephone number of the Offeror. (3) The Offeror’s Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) (4) Information necessary to evaluate the factors contained in the provision at 52.212-2 (5) Responses to provisions that require Offeror completion of information, representations, and certifications (other than those collected via the System for Award Management (SAM)); and (6) A statement specifying the extent of agreement with all terms, conditions, and provisions included in the solicitation and any solicitation amendments. Period for acceptance of offers. The Offeror agrees to hold the prices in its offer firm for 60 calendar days from the date specified for receipt of offers, unless another time period is specified in an addendum to the solicitation. The United States Coast Guard Training Center Birmingham-Southern is seeking to purchase a seven-month rental of one 6,000-pound LPG forklift and one 12,000-pound LPG forklift, including delivery, maintenance, repairs, replacement support, training, and LPG fuel support. All interested companies must provide quotation(s) for the following: CLIN 0001 — 6,000-Pound Forklift Rental. The contractor shall provide one 6,000-pound LPG forklift for a seven-month rental period. The unit of measure is month, and the quantity is seven months. The monthly price shall include delivery, setup, acceptance inspection, manuals, load chart, preventive maintenance, repairs, replacement parts, tires, replacement forklift support when required, required service reports, training, and removal at the end of the contract. This CLIN supports SOW Task One, Task Two, Task Three, Task Five, and Task Six. The contractor shall include all costs for delivery, setup, maintenance, repairs, replacement forklifts, initial training, one additional training session, reports, and removal in the monthly prices for CLIN 0001. The Government will not pay separate charges for those services. CLIN 0002 — 12,000-Pound Forklift Rental. The contractor shall provide one 12,000-pound LPG forklift for a seven-month rental period. The unit of measure is month, and the quantity is seven months. The monthly price shall include delivery, setup, acceptance inspection, manuals, load chart, preventive maintenance, repairs, replacement parts, tires, replacement forklift support when required, required service reports, training, and removal at the end of the contract. This CLIN supports SOW Task One, Task Two, Task Three, Task Five, and Task Six. The contractor shall include all costs for delivery, setup, maintenance, repairs, replacement forklifts, initial training, one additional training session, reports, and removal in the monthly prices for CLIN 0002. The Government will not pay separate charges for those services. CLIN 0003 — LPG Fuel. The contractor shall provide LPG fuel as requested by the Government. The unit of measure is gallon. The estimated quantity and maximum dollar amount will be inserted by the Government before solicitation release. The contractor shall provide a fixed price per gallon. The Government will pay only for the actual gallons delivered and verified by signed fuel delivery tickets. The total amount paid under this CLIN shall not exceed the stated maximum dollar amount. This CLIN supports SOW Task Four. Offerors are required to provide prices for all items/CLINs. A zero-dollar figure ($0.00) unit price means the offeror shall provide the service/supply at no charge to the Government. Unit prices left blank or annotated with something other than a dollar figure will be considered unacceptable. Reference Attached Statement of Work in Solicitation 75110PR270000099. Period Of Performance. The period of performance for this contract is December 1, 2026 thru June 30, 2027 Place of Performance. United States Coast Guard Training Center (TRACEN) Birmingham-Southern, 900 Arkadelphia Road, Birmingham, AL 35204. Basis for Award The following factors will be used to evaluate offers. The Government will make award to the responsible offeror submitting the lowest-priced quotation that is rated Technically Acceptable. If the lowest-priced quotation is rated Technically Unacceptable, the Government will evaluate the next lowest-priced quotation. This process will continue as necessary. Technical Acceptability: To be rated technically acceptable, the quotation shall include the following: (a) Proposed Equipment Information. The offeror shall identify the manufacturer, make, and model of the proposed 6,000-pound forklift and 12,000-pound forklift. (b) Equipment Specification Documentation. The offeror shall provide manufacturer specification sheets, product literature, or equivalent documentation showing that each proposed forklift meets all requirements in Sections 2.1.1 and 2.1.2 of the Statement of Work. The documentation shall show, at a minimum, rated capacity, load center, fuel type, mast height, tire type, fork length, side-shift capability, and required safety equipment. (c) Delivery Commitment. The offeror shall provide a written statement confirming that both proposed forklifts, meeting all Statement of Work requirements, will be available for delivery and commissioning at USCG TRACEN Birmingham-Southern no later than December 1, 2026. (e) Service and Support Plan. The offeror shall provide a brief plan describing how it will perform the required maintenance, repair, replacement, LPG fuel delivery, and training services. The plan shall confirm the offeror’s ability to meet the timeframes stated in the Statement of Work, including: (1) Preventive maintenance at manufacturer-recommended intervals; (2) Replacement equipment, when required, within four business days after Government notification; (3) On-site LPG fuel replenishment within two business days after Government request; (4) Initial training within five business days after delivery and commissioning; and (5) Additional training, when requested, within 10 business days after Government request. A quotation will be rated Technically Acceptable when it includes all required information and clearly shows that the proposed equipment and services meet the Statement of Work requirements. A quotation will be rated Technically Unacceptable when it fails to provide the required information, proposes equipment that does not meet the Statement of Work requirements, does not commit to the required delivery date, takes exception to a material requirement, or otherwise fails to show compliance with the Statement of Work. Price: The Government will evaluate the total evaluated price of each quotation. The total evaluated price will be the sum of: (a) All firm-fixed-price Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs) for the seven-month rental period, including equipment delivery, commissioning, rental, preventive maintenance, repairs, replacement equipment, training, and equipment removal; and (b) The full not-to-exceed amount of the liquid propane gas (LPG) fuel CLIN. The Government will evaluate prices for completeness, accuracy, and reasonableness. The Government may correct obvious arithmetic errors when calculating the total evaluated price. A quote must comply in all aspects with the requirements and conditions set forth in this RFQ; a quote must meet or exceed all mandatory RFQ requirements. If an Offeror takes exception to any of the terms and conditions of the RFQ or fails to meet any of the requirements of the RFQ, then the Government may consider the quote unacceptable A Firm-Fixed Price contract will be awarded to the responsible offeror whose offer fully conforms to this solicitation and is determined to be the most advantageous, considering price and other factors. The Government intends to evaluate offers and award a contract without discussions with Offerors. Therefore, the Offeror’s initial offer should contain the Offeror’s best terms. However, the Government reserves the right to conduct discussions, if necessary. The Government may reject any or all offers if such action is in the public interest, accept other than the lowest offer, and waive informalities and minor irregularities in offers received. The anticipated award date is 10 days after solicitation closing date. Only one purchase order is anticipated resulting from this RFQ, however the Government reserves the right to withdraw, modify, or eliminate various aspects of the requirement determined to be too costly or impractical prior to award.

postings.description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), MH-60 PMA-299 (AIR – 2.3.4.2), Patuxent River, MD intends to negotiate multiple sole-source orders over a five-period (FY27-FY31) under Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) N00019-26-G-1012 with Thales Defense & Security, Inc. (TDSI), 22605 Gateway Center Dr Clarksburg, MD 20871, to support product support, development, sustaining engineering, repairs, spares, and logistical services associated with the AN/AQS-22 Airborne Low Frequency Sonar (ALFS) system for integration into MH-60R, Multi-Mission Helicopter. This notice also publicizes the government’s intent to negotiate and award the first planned task order under this BOA. This initial order will require a Sustaining Engineering evaluation for three (3) separate Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) Specialized Test Equipment (STE) benches. The Government intends to negotiate the initial and all subsequent BOA orders with TDSI under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. This notice is published to identify interested responsible sources and obtain information regarding their capability to meet the stated requirement. The Government will consider timely submissions in determining whether a source is capable of meeting the requirement to satisfy FAR Part 10 and DFARS206.103-170. This notice also serves as the pre-solicitation synopsis requirements of FAR Part 5 for the initial task order. Future orders under the BOA will be synopsized individually as they arise. issued 2.0 REQUIREMENT DESCRIPTION 2.1 Overarching BOA Scope The anticipated orders issued under BOA N000926G1012 will encompass product support, Non-Recurring Engineering (NRE), development, and sustaining engineering supplies and services required to support the MH-60R Mission System AN/AQS-22 Airborne Low Frequency Sonar (ALFS) Weapon Replaceable Assemblies (WRAs). The primary WRAs include: Transducer Assembly (TA) Reeling Machine (RM) Reeling Machine Interface Unit (RMIU) Reeling Machine Control Unit (RMCU) Reel and Cable (R&C) The five-year scope includes NRE, recurring services, material, component repair, and logistical support to sustain and mitigate obsolescence across both active and delivered systems for the U.S. Navy and Foreign Military Sales (FMS) customers. 2.2 First Planned Task Order Scope The initial order to be executed under the BOA requires a Sustaining Engineering evaluation for the three (3) specific GFE STE benches associated with the AN/AQS-22 ALFS program: Reeling Machine Test Bench (RMTB) Transducer Assembly Test Bench (TATB) Reeling Machine Control System Test Bench (RMCSTB) This effort comprises engineering evaluations, hardware/software analysis, and documentation support to establish the test bench baseline configuration and Technical Data Package (TDP) for each bench., 3.0 SOLE SOURCE JUSTIFICATION This acquisition is being pursued on a sole-source basis under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) (formerly 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1)), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1, "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." TDSI is the U.S. based subsidiary of Thales Underwater Systems SAS (TUS), the original designer, developer, and manufacturer of the AN/AQS-22 ALFS System Weapon Replaceable Assemblies (WRAs) for the Transducer Assembly (TA), Reeling Machine (RM), Reeling Machine Interface Unit (RMIU), Reeling Machine Control Unit (RMCU) and Reel and Cable (R&C). TUS owns the proprietary data for these WRAs that is required to perform the efforts herein, including the applicable specifications, source code, and drawings. Thus, TDSI has access and rights to the proprietary drawings and data required to perform these efforts efficiently and effectively. TDSI is also the current repair facility for TAs and the only source with domestic facilities, data, and experience to complete these efforts. No other firm possesses the required knowledge, experience, expertise, and proprietary technical and software data packages required to successfully fulfill this order in a timely and cost-effective manner. 4.0 SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS (CAPABILITY STATEMENT) Responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which will be considered by the agency. Any offer must clearly demonstrate the capability to respond to this requirement without detriment to the H-60 Helicopter Program and must include personnel/resources specifically qualified to provide the supplies/services described. The capability statement must include your approach to accomplish this effort in support of the H-60 Helicopter Program. This notice is not a request for proposals and does not imply or promise that the Government intends to award a contract vehicle as a result of this notice or in response to any capability statements received. The Government will not reimburse any costs incurred to prepare responses to this notice. It is requested that interested businesses submit to the contracting office a brief capabilities statement package (no more than 12 pages in length, single-spaced, 12-point font minimum) demonstrating ability to perform the tasking listed under the required capabilities. Capabilities Statement shall address both ALFS and MTS in one document. This documentation must address at a minimum the following: Company Name; Company Address; Company Business Size, and Point-of-Contact (POC) name, phone number, fax number, and e-mail address. Company profile to include number of employees, annual revenue history, office location(s), UEI number, and a statement regarding current small/large business status. Prior/current corporate experience performing efforts of similar size and scope to the tasking described under “Required Capabilities” within the last three years, including contract numbers, contract values, Government point of contract with current telephone number, and a brief description of how the referenced contract related to those tasks. Management approach to staffing this effort with qualified personnel. Statement regarding capability to obtain the required industrial security clearances for personnel. Company's ability to begin performance upon contract award. What type of work has your company performed in the past in support of the same or similar requirement? Can or has your company managed a task of this nature? If so, please provide details. Can or has your company managed a team of subcontractors before? If so, please cite contracts and teaming arrangement. What specific technical skills does your company possess which ensures capability to perform the tasks? If you are a small business, provide an explanation of your company's ability to perform at least 50% of the tasking described in required capabilities. Provide a statement including current small/large business status and company profile to include number of employees, annual revenue history, office location, CAGE code, UEI number, etc. Respondents to this notice must also indicate whether they are a large business or qualify as a Small, Small Disadvantaged, Small Disadvantaged Veteran Owned Small Business Women-Owned, 8(a), Hub Zone, or Service Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business Concern. Include in your response your ability to meet the requirements in the Facility and Safeguarding requirements. Your response to this Sources Sought, including any capabilities statement, shall be electronically submitted via email to morgan.p.mckay.civ@us.navy.mil, in either Microsoft Word or Portable Document Format (PDF). The deadline for response to this request is 4:00 p.m., Eastern Daylight Time, 28 November 2026. All data received in response to this Sources Sought that is marked or designated as corporate or proprietary will be protected. Information and materials submitted in response to this request WILL NOT be returned. Classified material SHALL NOT be submitted. No phone calls will be accepted. All questions must be submitted via e-mail. The Government is not committed nor obligated to pay for the information provided, and no basis for claims against the Government shall arise as a result of a response to these Sources Sought. 5.0 SUBCONTRACTING OPPORTUNITIES Firms interested in potential subcontracting opportunities related to this effort are encouraged to contact TDSI directly to inquire about partnering opportunities. 6.0 DISCLAIMER THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. IT IS A MARKET RESEARCH TOOL BEING USED TO DETERMINE POTENTIAL AND ELIGIBLE BUSINESSES CAPABLE OF PROVIDING THE SUPPLIES/SERVICES DESCRIBED HEREIN PRIOR TO DETERMINING THE METHOD OF ACQUISITION AND ISSUANCE OF A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. THE GOVERNMENT IS NOT COMMITTED NOR OBLIGATED TO PAY FOR THE INFORMATION PROVIDED, AND NO BASIS FOR CLAIMS AGAINST THE GOVERNMENT SHALL ARISE AS A RESULT OF A RESPONSE TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY.

postings.description: Sources Sought Announcement FMF EC B-HAC Insular Air-Naval Station Hanger Renovation & Facilities Expansion U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) – Latin America and Caribbean District (SAA) ****SOURCES SOUGHT FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY**** This announcement seeks information from industry which will be used for preliminary planning purposes. No proposals are being requested or accepted with this announcement. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SYNOPSIS. NO SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS OR DRAWINGS ARE AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. 1. AGENCY: United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Latin America and Caribbean District (SAA) 2. NAICS: 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction 3. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: Insular Air-Naval Station (Estación Aeronaval Insular), San Cristobal Island, Galapagos Province, Ecuador. 4. ACQUISITION INFORMATION: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Latin America and Caribbean District (SAA), is issuing this Sources Sought announcement to identify qualified, capable, and interested U.S. firms eligible to serve as prime contractors for a potential multi-phase Design-Build construction project at the Insular Air-Naval Station on San Cristóbal Island, Galápagos, Ecuador. The project is funded through Foreign Military Financing (FMF) and is subject to applicable Offshore Procurement (OSP) requirements. The anticipated acquisition will require an eligible U.S. firm to serve as the prime contractor, unless an exception or waiver is separately authorized by the appropriate approval authority. The results of this market research will inform the Government's acquisition strategy, procurement approach, assessment of U.S. contractor capabilities and interest, and evaluation of applicable OSP requirements. Limited U.S. contractor participation or competition does not, by itself, constitute approval of or establish entitlement to an OSP waiver. Any exception or waiver would require a separate determination and approval in accordance with applicable policies and procedures. Anticipated Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Design-Build (C-Contract) with a base requirement and option phases. Estimated Magnitude of Construction: $7million to $9 million Performance Period: 540 days after Notice to Proceed. Anticipated Award Date: Fiscal Year 2027 Quarter 3 In accordance with FAR 19.000(b)(1)(ii), the Procuring Contracting Officer (PCO) has elected not to apply FAR Part 19 (Small Business Programs) to this overseas procurement. Consequently, small business set-asides will not be utilized for this project in the Galapagos Islands, Ecuador. However, because this project is funded by Foreign Military Financing (FMF), standard statutory constraints require procurement from U.S. sources. All responsible U.S. sources—including both large and small business concerns—are highly encouraged to submit capabilities statements in response to this notice. The results of this market research will inform the Government's acquisition strategy, procurement approach, assessment of U.S. contractor capabilities and interest, and evaluation of applicable OSP requirements. Limited U.S. contractor participation or competition does not, by itself, constitute approval of or establish entitlement to an OSP waiver. Any exception or waiver would require a separate determination and approval in accordance with applicable policies and procedures. Foreign Military Financing (FMF) and Offshore Procurement (OSP): In accordance with Section 42(c) of the Arms Export Control Act (22 U.S.C. § 2791(c)), award is restricted to eligible U.S. firms, as an OSP determination has not been approved. The Government reserves the right to pursue an OSP determination if deemed in its best interest. U.S. prime contractors may utilize qualified local subcontractors, subject to applicable FMF and procurement requirements. 5. ANTICIPATED ACQUISITION STRATEGY: The final acquisition strategy will be determined based on the responses received from this Sources Sought notice, contractor availability, and stakeholder coordination. The Government is contemplating the following acquisition approaches: Primary Approach (Best Value Trade-Off (BVTO) Design-Build C-Contract with Options): Award a single Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Design-Build construction contract through a competitive Request for Proposals (RFP), utilizing a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) source selection approach, with options subject to funding availability. Base Requirement (Phases 1 & 2): Phase 1 – Hangar Renovation: Renovation and modernization of the existing aviation hangar to support Bell 430 rescue helicopters and Beechcraft King Air 350 aircraft. Phase 2 – Fuel Farm: Design and construction of a new fuel farm using a Design-Build-to-Budget (DB2B) approach, including demolition of the existing fuel facility. Option Package (Phase 3): Phase 3 – New Hangar: Design and construction of a new aviation hangar to support King Air 350 aircraft, exercisable based on funding availability and operational priorities. Offshore Procurement (OSP) Strategy Determination: U.S. Contractor Only Competition: If market research demonstrates sufficient interest and capability from responsible U.S. contractors capable of executing works in the Galapagos Islands, the solicitation may be restricted to U.S. firms in compliance with standard FMF guidelines. OSP Waiver / Unrestricted Competition: If responses indicate limited U.S. industry interest, severe logistical/cost premiums, or inadequate competition, USACE will utilize the findings of this market research to justify and process an FMF Offshore Procurement Waiver to allow foreign/host-nation firms to compete. 6. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The contemplated scope consists of complete Design-Build to Budget (DB2B) services to include civil, geotechnical, structural, architectural, MEP (mechanical, electrical, plumbing), specialized fire suppression, aircraft maintenance utility integration, fuel containment/dispensing, demolition, and environmental protection compliant with both U.S. engineering standards (Unified Facilities Criteria - UFC) and host-nation Galapagos environmental regulations. The project is divided into three distinct phases of development. The Government has developed preliminary design documents to support the proposed requirements, which will serve as the basis for the contemplated Design-Build acquisition. The selected Design-Build contractor is anticipated to be responsible for completing the design and performing construction in accordance with the final contract requirements. Project Phase Phase 1 (Base) Primary Function/Facility: Existing Hangar Renovation (Supporting Bell 430 Rescue Helicopter & King Air 350) Key Technical Considerations: Design/Build (30%) documents for Renovation to the existing hanger for the Bell 430 rescue helicopter and King Air 350. Phase 2 (Base) Primary Function/Facility: New Aviation Fuel Farm & Legacy Demolition Key Technical Considerations: Design/Build (65%) documents for a new Fuel Farm and demo of the existing fuel farm Phase 3 (Option) Primary Function/Facility: New Aircraft Hangar (Supporting King Air SKA 350) Key Technical Considerations: Design/Build (65%) documents for a new Hangar for a new King Air SKA 3350 7. SOURCES SOUGHT: The purpose of this source sought is to gain knowledge of interest, capabilities and qualifications of contractors who have the capabilities to complete and perform contracts of this magnitude, and to address any questions, recommendations or concerns from Industry. The Government must ensure there is adequate competition among potential pool of responsible contractors. Prior Government contract work is not required for submitting a response under this Sources Sought announcement. The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. 8. RESPONSES: The Capabilities Statement for this Sources Sought is not intended to be a Request for Proposal nor Invitation for Bid, nor does it restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach. It is to request statements regarding the company's ability to demonstrate existing-or-developed expertise and experience in relation to the areas specified herein. Any commercial brochures or currently existing marketing material may also be submitted. This synopsis is for information and planning purposes only and is neither to be construed as a commitment by the Government nor will the Government pay for information solicited. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. Interested parties are requested to provide a capabilities statement addressing the following areas. Section 1: Company Information Company Name, Address, and Website Point of Contact (Name, Title, Phone, Email) CAGE Code and SAM UEI Number Business Size and Status (e.g., Small Business, Large Business) Bonding: What bonding or guarantee methods are available to your company to secure contract performance and protect downstream subcontractor/labor payments for a project located in Ecuador? Please specify if your company utilizes US Treasury-listed Surety Bonds, Ecuadorian Bank Letters of Guarantee (Carta Fianza), or Insurance-backed Guarantees (Póliza de Caución). Relevant NAICS Codes Is your company a U.S.-based firm interested in participating as the prime contractor for this project? (Yes/No) Section 2: Interest and Experience in Ecuador Please confirm your company's interest in performing a design-build construction project of this magnitude and complexity in Galapagos Province, Ecuador or similar remote area. Summary of prior construction experience in Ecuador or South America. Address our minimum operational needs of experience with: Ecuadorian construction standards (Código Ecuatoriano de la Construcción), professional licensing requirements (Colegio de Ingenieros del Ecuador / Colegio de Arquitectos del Ecuador); Local labor laws, and tax/customs processes (SENAE and SRI). Describe your firm's capability to obtain the necessary permits and licenses required for construction work in Ecuador and to comply with all applicable host nation laws and regulations. Discuss your firm's experience with international logistics, including the transportation of materials and equipment to project sites in South America. Discuss your firm’s familiarity with base security clearance procedures, host-nation military vetting, and port access protocols. Section 3: Design-Build Qualifications and Technical Capabilities Interested firms are requested to provide information demonstrating their qualifications, relevant experience, and technical capabilities to execute the proposed multi-phase Design-Build (D-B) construction project. 3.1 Design-Build Qualifications and Relevant Experience Provide a brief overview of your firm's Design-Build experience as a prime contractor. Describe your firm's proposed D-B delivery approach, including the use of in-house design capabilities, joint ventures, or partnerships with qualified U.S., Ecuadorian, or international Architect-Engineer (A-E) firms. Provide up to three (3) examples of relevant Design-Build construction projects completed within the past five (5) years. For each project, identify the project name, location, contract value, year completed, scope of work, and your firm's role as prime contractor, joint venture partner, or subcontractor. Projects involving aviation facilities, aircraft hangars, warehouses, logistics facilities, military installations, fuel systems, or construction in remote locations are particularly relevant. 3.2 Specialized Aviation Fuel Facility Experience Describe your firm's experience designing, constructing, renovating, or upgrading aviation fuel storage and distribution facilities, including: Fuel storage tanks, pumping and transfer systems, and associated piping. Secondary containment, spill prevention, and environmental protection systems. Compliance with applicable safety and technical standards, specialized testing, and commissioning. Identify whether specialized aviation fuel system work would be performed using in-house resources or qualified specialty subcontractors. 3.3 Logistics and Local Execution Capabilities Provide an overview of your firm's proposed approach to executing construction on San Cristóbal Island, Galápagos, Ecuador, addressing the following: Material Procurement and Staging: Proposed sourcing, procurement, and staging of construction materials and specialized equipment in Guayaquil, Ecuador, or other suitable locations. Maritime Transportation and Port Operations: Proposed shipping routes, port-of-entry operations, and cargo handling at Puerto Baquerizo Moreno, San Cristóbal Island, or other suitable locations, subject to applicable host-nation, port, military installation, and security requirements. On-Island Transportation: Approach for transporting heavy construction materials and equipment from the port to the project site. Local Workforce and Subcontracting: Availability of qualified local subcontractors, specialty trades, and skilled labor, including anticipated use of U.S. and local resources. Environmental and Biosecurity Requirements: Experience addressing environmental restrictions, permitting, customs, and biosecurity requirements associated with construction in remote or environmentally sensitive locations. Logistical Challenges and Risk Mitigation: Identify anticipated logistical challenges and proposed strategies to minimize cost, schedule, and execution risks. Section 4: Market Research and Acquisition Considerations The Government seeks industry feedback to evaluate the feasibility of the proposed requirements, anticipated construction costs, performance period, acquisition strategy, and potential barriers to U.S. contractor participation. 4.1 Construction Cost and Market Conditions Based on your firm's experience, is the estimated construction magnitude of $7.181 million reasonable for the proposed scope and location? If not, explain the anticipated cost differences. What major cost drivers or premiums would you anticipate for construction in the Galápagos Islands, including shipping, equipment mobilization, labor, materials, and specialized subcontractors? Identify significant market conditions, such as local labor availability, supply chain limitations, and subcontractor capacity in Ecuador, that may affect project execution. 4.2 Schedule Feasibility and Execution Risks Is the proposed 540-calendar-day period of performance achievable for the base contract requirements, considering design, procurement, permitting, mobilization, construction, testing, and commissioning? What significant technical, logistical, environmental, or regulatory risks could affect successful project execution? What schedule adjustments or risk mitigation measures would you recommend improving project feasibility? 4.3 Offshore Procurement (OSP) and U.S. Contractor Participation Considering applicable Foreign Military Financing (FMF) and Offshore Procurement (OSP) requirements, what challenges could affect your firm's ability to compete and execute the project as a U.S. prime contractor? Describe anticipated reliance on U.S. versus non-U.S. materials, equipment, labor, and subcontractors, and identify any significant cost or logistical implications. What contracting arrangements, supply chain strategies, or industry partnerships would your firm consider supporting compliance with applicable OSP requirements? Responses will support the Government's market research and assessment of applicable procurement requirements. Any OSP exception or waiver would require a separate determination and approval by the appropriate authority. 4.4 Acquisition Strategy and Industry Interest What adjustments to the proposed acquisition strategy, project scope, phasing, or schedule would increase your firm's likelihood of submitting a proposal? Would your firm be interested in competing for a single Design-Build contract with a base requirement and additional optional phases? Would your firm be interested in participating in a virtual industry day to discuss the proposed requirements, project location, and anticipated acquisition strategy? 9.
